findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and can't be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` and its body is just `pass`. That leaves four abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` (processors/detector.py:142-164) and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (processors/detector.py:166-170). `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at this class (grouptype.py:27), and `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates it with `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (models/detector.py:86). So for any Detector with `type="metric_alert_fire"`, reading `detector.detector_handler` now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Before this change the handler returned `[]` from `evaluate`. Nothing in `src/` calls `process_detectors` today, so this doesn't break anything yet. It will break `process_detectors` as soon as a metric-alert detector reaches it. Either keep stub implementations for now (`counter_names = []`, and the getters returning 0 and `{}`, plus a `build_occurrence_and_event_data` that raises `NotImplementedError`), or don't register the handler on `MetricAlertFire` until it exists. The TODO on line 10 ("will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction") is also out of date now.

findings.title: Occurrence assertions only compare a hard-coded id, so fingerprint, priority and type go unchecked
findings.body:
`IssueOccurrence.__eq__` compares only `id` (src/sentry/issues/issue_occurrence.py:181-184). `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` always uses `id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578"`, so every occurrence assertion in this file passes no matter which fingerprint, `initial_issue_priority` or type the handler produced. Concrete cases that pass by accident:
- `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` (lines 536-545) builds the expected occurrence for group key `"val1"` while the code under test evaluates `"group_key"`. The fingerprints differ (`<id>:val1` vs `<id>:group_key`) and the test still passes.
- `test_state_results_multi_group` (lines 179-222): `occurrence` and `occurrence_2` compare equal to each other. `assert_has_calls(..., any_order=True)` would therefore pass even if both produced calls were for `group_1`.

The main new behaviour, passing `PriorityLevel(new_status)` through to the occurrence, is never verified. Fix: compare `occurrence.to_dict()` (or the individual fields) in the assertions, or derive the mock id from the group key so occurrences for different keys don't compare equal. Then correct the `"val1"` argument in the `test_dedupe` case.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `evaluate` now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the docstring still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.

contracts.action: MetricAlertDetectorHandler switched from DetectorHandler (with an evaluate that returned []) to an empty subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler
contracts.equivalent_path: Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self); the test MockDetectorStateHandler is a StatefulDetectorHandler that implements every abstract member
contracts.before_after: Before: instantiating worked and evaluate returned []. After: the class has abstract members left, so instantiating it raises TypeError.
contracts.visible_effect: No production caller of process_detectors or detector_handler exists in src/ today, so no effect yet. A future caller will get a TypeError for metric_alert_fire detectors.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError raised from the Detector.detector_handler property, uncaught in process_detectors

contracts.action: evaluate_group_key_value calls the new abstract hook build_occurrence_and_event_data for non-OK status changes, and the result is produced to Kafka
contracts.equivalent_path: The OK branch builds a StatusChangeMessage with the fingerprint and project_id; create_issue_occurrence_from_result sends IssueOccurrence results as PayloadType.OCCURRENCE together with event_data
contracts.before_after: Before: non-OK changes returned result=None and nothing was produced. After: the hook's occurrence and event_data are produced via produce_occurrence_to_kafka.
contracts.visible_effect: Issues get created on the issue platform for detectors that fire
contracts.failure_mode: An exception in the hook propagates out of process_detectors before commit_state_updates runs, so state is not committed and the packet will be reprocessed

contracts.action: New Detector.group_type property, which wraps registry.get_by_slug
contracts.before_after: Same lookup, now behind a property; detector_handler uses it
contracts.failure_mode: Returns None for an unknown slug; detector_handler logs an error and returns None as before

summary: The PR adds a `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook so the stateful detector can produce occurrences, and changes `evaluate` to return a dict keyed by group key. There are three findings: two at "fix" and one at "consider". First, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is now an empty subclass of an abstract class, so building a handler for a `metric_alert_fire` detector raises TypeError; nothing in `src/` calls it yet. Second, the new tests compare occurrences only by a hard-coded id, so fingerprint, priority and type are never checked, and at least one test passes with a mismatched group key. Third, the `evaluate` docstring still says it returns a list.
